# LBS Network Variants

Also called: Backward LBS, Deterministic SMPL skinning, Learned forward LBS

## Overview
This family explores alternative mechanisms for computing skinning weights and deformations in Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) for Gaussian Splatting, specifically comparing learned networks against deterministic template-based approaches. It addresses the limitations of fixed skinning weights by investigating whether conditioning on pose or using learned mappings improves reconstruction quality and reduces artifacts in animatable human avatars.

## Shared principles
All variants in this family operate within the framework of Linear Blend Skinning for Gaussian Splatting, where canonical 3D Gaussians are deformed using precomputed rigid joint transformations and learnable or deterministic skinning weights. The core objective is to map points from the canonical space to the posed space while maintaining geometric consistency and visual fidelity.

A key distinction in the implementation of these variants involves the handling of global transformations. For backward LBS, the query points are canonicalized using the SMPL global translation and rotation before being processed by the LBS network [S1]. This ensures that the local pose conditioning is applied relative to a consistent global frame.

The performance of these variants is evaluated using Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) on standard datasets. The reported metrics indicate that learned forward LBS achieves the highest quality, followed by deterministic SMPL weights, with backward LBS yielding the lowest PSNR among the three [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Forward LBS Network](19756-forward-lbs-network.md)
The learned forward LBS network computes skinning weights directly as a function of the point's canonical position and the current pose. It is chosen for its ability to avoid discretized artifacts and handle points far from the surface effectively, achieving the highest PSNR of 31.6.

### Backward LBS
Backward LBS conditions the skinning weight network on the local body poses $\theta$. The query points are canonicalized using the SMPL global translation and rotation before querying the network [S1]. This variant suffers from difficulties in learning skinning weights for points far from the surface, resulting in artifacts under specific poses, and achieves a PSNR of 29.5 [S1].

### Deterministic SMPL weights
This variant uses nearest neighbor SMPL skinning weights derived from the template mesh. While it avoids the training complexity of a network, it causes discretized artifacts on the cloth surface due to the discrete nature of the template weights, achieving a PSNR of 30.5 [S1].

## Background
The comparison of these variants originates from the ARAH (Animatable Volume Rendering of Articulated Human SDFs) paper, which ablates different LBS strategies to determine the optimal deformation method for Gaussian Splatting-based avatars [S1]. The study highlights the trade-offs between learned flexibility and deterministic stability in skinning weight computation.
